scope: Retrospective inventory of model-safety stops that affected the NTSD 2.4 native-port project (repo ntsd-2.4). Built from the project's own refusal register and study docs, from Codex rollout logs (~/.codex/sessions) and Claude Code transcripts (~/.claude/projects). Records only product error/notice text and the project's own operation-category labels. No rejected output, prompt or triggering tool call is reconstructed. The register itself states the exact trigger of each event is unknown and that a saved error proves neither a user violation nor that the decision was wrong.
method_notes: Codex: only top-level event_msg/task_complete records whose structured payload carried codex_error_info were counted as real events; occurrences inside custom_tool_call / custom_tool_call_output / compaction records are agents reading logs and were excluded.
Codex tool refusals (Computer Use, web) were read from the tool-output record and attributed to the issuing call; app id and cwd preserved, no tool input text kept.
Claude Code: only assistant records with message.stop_reason == 'refusal' and client-inserted system/user-meta notices were counted; tool_result echoes were excluded.
Timestamps are UTC. blocked_hours is the span a dependent path was held, not a claim the incident itself was 'resolved' — the project keeps every incident open.

incidents.operation_category: Network-play integration (N2): routing the window 0x401 notification into OriginalNetworkNotification during two-app LAN match work

incidents.project_response: Refusal preserved in a dedicated record (public messages, request/message ids, line); affected operation not retried or rerouted; the active /loop was stopped; last visible progress noted with causalityEstablished=false. User deferred networking the same day; N1 kept committed, partial N2 preserved uncommitted.
incidents.resolution: Deferred by user 2026-10-01 (committed 19:30Z). On 2026-10-02 the user lifted the deferral and removed the blanket N2-N5 hold as 'an unsupported interpretation of the saved incident'; networking N1-N5 was then implemented and independently reviewed to a full localhost Naruto/Sasuke match (commits 2026-10-02). incidents.no_reroute_note: The immediate documented handling followed the rule strictly: deferred, preserved, loop stopped, no retry/reroute of the refused operation. The later completion is where the records are ambiguous: after the user lifted the hold, a different agent/model (Codex gpt-6-astra, session 01a0f597) implemented N2-N5 — the same broad task Claude had refused to continue. The project frames this as user-directed re-scoping (only the unknown specific operation stays blocked, not all networking), not as rerouting; but because the exact refused operation is unknown, the records cannot establish the new work did not re-execute it.
incidents.characterization: Record: exactBlockedOutputAvailable=false, exactTriggerKnown=false; 'nearby file reads do not establish the cause.' NETWORK_PLAY.md: incident 'preserved without treating it as evidence that all network integration is prohibited.' Not called a false positive by the records.
